seleccion.titulo: Gene-edited porcine liver xenotransplantation: advances and key clinical translation barriers
seleccion.resumen_previo: Una revisión en revista de primera línea analiza los avances recientes en xenotrasplante hepático porcino, incluyendo edición multigénica e inmunosupresión optimizada, basándose en resultados de primates no humanos y estudios clínicos. El trabajo sintetiza las barreras clave para la traducción clínica de esta terapia dirigida a resolver la escasez global de hígados donantes.
seleccion.extracto: Liver allotransplantation constitutes a vital organ-replacement therapy for end-stage liver disease, yet the global shortage of donor livers severely limits treatment capacity. Porcine liver xenotransplantation, which employs genetically edited pig livers as grafts, holds promise for alleviating donor scarcity and providing bridging organ support for patients with acute liver failure. In recent years, considerable progress has been achieved in preclinical non-human primate (NHP) models and human clinical studies. seleccion.titulo: Corneal Xenotransplantation: Lessons From Allograft Immunobiology and Emerging Translational Strategies
seleccion.resumen_previo: Una revisión en la revista Xenotransplantation analiza cómo los mecanismos de rechazo inmunológico en xenotrasplantes de córnea difieren de los alotrasplantes, extrayendo lecciones clínicas para traducir esta técnica a pacientes. El trabajo aborda un obstáculo central para expandir el acceso global a trasplantes corneales mediante órganos animales modificados.
seleccion.extracto: ABSTRACT Corneal transplantation is an effective sight‐restoring procedure, yet its global impact remains constrained by limited and uneven access to human donor tissue and by immune‐mediated graft failure, particularly in high‐risk recipients. Xenotransplantation offers a potentially scalable alternative, but successful clinical translation requires an understanding of how xenogeneic immune responses differ from, and build upon, the mechanisms governing corneal allograft rejection. seleccion.titulo: Biomedical properties and emerging translational potential of bovine milk extracellular vesicles
seleccion.resumen_previo: Un estudio examina vesículas extracelulares derivadas de leche bovina como plataforma biocompatible para aplicaciones terapéuticas y diagnósticas. Aunque toca biotecnología de origen animal, no se enfoca en xenotrasplante de órganos y constituye una mención tangencial al campo.
seleccion.extracto: Extracellular vesicles have garnered significant attention in the biomedical field due to their potential as therapeutic agents and diagnostic tools. Bovine milk extracellular vesicles (BMEVs), in particular, have emerged as a promising tool in biomedical research due to their unique biocompatibility, stability, and ease of isolation. As an alternative to extracellular vesicles sourced from human cells, such as stem cells or blood, these naturally occurring nanovesicles are increasingly recognized for their dual role as potential therapeutic carriers and diagnostic candidates. seleccion.titulo: Cross-species structure–mechanics prediction in the intervertebral disc
seleccion.resumen_previo: Un preprint desarrolla un marco computacional para comparar la estructura y función mecánica de discos intervertebrales entre ratas, minicerdos y humanos. Si bien utiliza modelos animales porcinos, el trabajo es de biología comparativa general sin relación explícita a xenotrasplante clínico.
seleccion.extracto: Despite long-standing uncertainty regarding the suitability of animal intervertebral disc (IVD) models for the study of human IVD pathophysiology, few cross-species studies have integrated hierarchical structure with mechanical function.
